Question: How did the viking's form of government differ from the other countries at the time?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends want to play a game together. Some kids decide everything together, like a group vote. Some kids have one big boss who tells everyone what to do. Some kids have rules made by grown-ups.

But the Vikings were different! They didn’t have a king or queen who told everyone what to do all the time. Instead, they had leaders called chieftains, who were like the strongest or smartest people in their group. The other Vikings could choose to follow them or not. Sometimes, they would talk together and decide things as a group, but not always the same way as other countries.

So, the Vikings’ way of deciding who leads and makes rules was a little bit different from other places back then!
